children: Factorial Energy posted revenue in the quarter, compared with none a year earlier, and swung to net income from a loss. The sale of its first commercial drone cells generated revenue; a gain from remeasuring Series A warrant liabilities lifted results, partly offset by higher selling, general and administrative costs and a $4.1 million arbitration judgment.
¹ Reported as “Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders - diluted”. ³ Reported as “Net income (loss) per share attributable to common stockholders - diluted”.
: Revenue came from the sale of the company’s first commercial drone cells.
: Expense fell 30.8%, primarily reflecting $2.6 million of joint-development partner reimbursements, partly offset by $0.8 million higher payroll and benefits.
: Included a $1.8 million inventory write-down to net realizable value, as well as labor, overhead and direct material costs for drone cells.
: Capital expenditures were $3.4 million in the first nine months; fiscal 2026 capital expenditures are expected to be $10.0 million to $12.0 million.
